rawItems.body:
Duolingo, Inc. (DUOL) closed the most recent trading day at $131.95, moving +1.72% from the previous trading session. This move outpaced the S&P 500's daily loss of 0.45%. On the other hand, the Dow registered a loss of 0.25%, and the technology-centric Nasdaq decreased by 1.16%.
The stock of company has risen by 9.97% in the past month, leading the Business Services sector's gain of 4.05% and the S&P 500's gain of 2.14%.
The investment community will be paying close attention to the earnings performance of Duolingo, Inc. in its upcoming release. The company is forecasted to report an EPS of $0.58, showcasing a 36.26% downward movement from the corresponding quarter of the prior year. Meanwhile, our latest consensus estimate is calling for revenue of $296.19 million, up 17.42% from the prior-year quarter.
Looking at the full year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates suggest analysts are expecting earnings of $2.76 per share and revenue of $1.21 billion. These totals would mark changes of -67.79% and +16.36%, respectively, from last year.
Investors should also take note of any recent adjustments to analyst estimates for Duolingo, Inc. These revisions help to show the ever-changing nature of near-term business trends. As such, positive estimate revisions reflect analyst optimism about the business and profitability.
Our research demonstrates that these adjustments in estimates directly associate with imminent stock price performance. To benefit from this, we have developed the Zacks Rank, a proprietary model which takes these estimate changes into account and provides an actionable rating system.
The Zacks Rank system, spanning from #1 (Strong Buy) to #5 (Strong Sell), boasts an impressive track record of outperformance, audited externally, with #1 ranked stocks yielding an average annual return of +25% since 1988. Over the past month, there's been no change in the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. Duolingo, Inc. is holding a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) right now.
Looking at its valuation, Duolingo, Inc. is holding a Forward P/E ratio of 46.97. This represents a premium compared to its industry average Forward P/E of 17.75.
We can additionally observe that DUOL currently boasts a PEG ratio of 1.01. The PEG ratio is similar to the widely-used P/E ratio, but this metric also takes the company's expected earnings growth rate into account. The Technology Services was holding an average PEG ratio of 1.53 at yesterday's closing price.
The Technology Services industry is part of the Business Services sector. With its current Zacks Industry Rank of 110, this industry ranks in the top 45% of all industries, numbering over 250.

rawItems.body:
Find winning stocks in any market cycle. Join 7 million investors using Simply Wall St's investing ideas for FREE.
Duolingo stock has given up a large part of its previous gains, with the share price down about 65.8% over the past year, yet the valuation checks still flag a mixed picture rather than a clear bargain or clear overvaluation.
-
Over the last 12 months, Duolingo has declined 65.8%, which puts recent pricing firmly in correction territory and raises the question of whether sentiment has swung too far.
-
On the fundamental side, expectations that Duolingo can keep growing its user base and improve monetization may support the equity story, while concerns about stalling daily active user momentum and the pace of converting engagement into revenue remain a key risk.
-
Across the broader checks, Duolingo scores 4 out of 6 on valuation, which points to a mixed set of signals rather than an obviously cheap or clearly expensive stock.
The stock's next move may depend on whether the current price already reflects those growth and engagement risks, or still incorporates too much optimism about the path ahead for Duolingo.
Find out why Duolingo's -65.8% return over the last year is lagging behind its peers.
Does Duolingo Look Pricey on Earnings?
P/E is a useful lens for Duolingo because the company is already generating earnings that can be compared against its share price. Duolingo currently trades at about 14.3x earnings, which sits below both the Consumer Services industry average P/E of 16.9x and the peer group average of 16.6x. On those simple comparisons, the stock does not screen as expensive relative to many similar businesses.
However, a more tailored assessment that factors in Duolingo's growth profile, margins, size and risk suggests a lower fair P/E of roughly 7.9x. That is a sizeable gap to the current 14.3x multiple, so on this framework the stock screens as overvalued even after the recent share price pullback. The recent concerns about daily active user momentum and monetization raised in analyst commentary underline why some investors may question paying a premium to that fair multiple.
Overall, Duolingo appears overvalued on the P/E multiple when set against the more customised fair ratio benchmark.
See what the numbers say about this price — find out in our valuation breakdown.
The Duolingo Narrative: What Would Justify Today's Price?
For Duolingo, Simply Wall St Narratives pick up where the valuation puzzle leaves off. They set out what kind of future path for growth, margins and earnings would need to play out for the stock to be worth materially more or less than today's price, and they sit on Simply Wall St's Community page. Rather than focusing on a single multiple or model result, each narrative lays out its underlying assumptions so you can compare them with Duolingo's reported results over time.

rawItems.title: Docebo (DCBO) Q1 Earnings: Taking a Look at Key Metrics Versus Estimates
rawItems.summary: Although the revenue and EPS for Docebo (DCBO) give a sense of how its business performed in the quarter ended March 2026, it might be worth considering how some key metrics compare with Wall Street estimates and the year-ago numbers.
rawItems.body:
Docebo Inc. (DCBO) reported $65.62 million in revenue for the quarter ended March 2026, representing a year-over-year increase of 14.5%. EPS of $0.34 for the same period compares to $0.27 a year ago.
The reported revenue compares to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $65.5 million, representing a surprise of +0.19%. The company delivered an EPS surprise of +2.01%, with the consensus EPS estimate being $0.33.
While investors scrutinize revenue and earnings changes year-over-year and how they compare with Wall Street expectations to determine their next move, some key metrics always offer a more accurate picture of a company's financial health.
As these metrics influence top- and bottom-line performance, comparing them to the year-ago numbers and what analysts estimated helps investors project a stock's price performance more accurately.
Here is how Docebo performed in the just reported quarter in terms of the metrics most widely monitored and projected by Wall Street analysts:
-
Annual Recurring Revenue: $248.9 million compared to the $247.06 million average estimate based on three analysts.
-
Customers: 3,578 versus the two-analyst average estimate of 3,464.
-
Revenue- Professional Services: $4.98 million versus the four-analyst average estimate of $4.25 million. The reported number represents a year-over-year change of +59.9%.
-
Revenue- Subscription Revenue: $60.64 million compared to the $61.27 million average estimate based on four analysts. The reported number represents a change of +11.9% year over year.
View all Key Company Metrics for Docebo here>>>
Shares of Docebo have returned +30.5% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +11% change. The stock currently has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), indicating that it could outperform the broader market in the near term.

rawItems.body:
Fair Isaac stock has more than doubled over the past five years, yet its current valuation sends mixed signals, with a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) intrinsic value estimate pointing to upside while traditional market multiples suggest the shares are on the expensive side.
Fair Isaac has delivered a 131.4% return over five years, which puts longer term shareholders in a strong position and raises the bar for what future returns would need to justify today's price.
Regulatory changes that open Fair Isaac's core mortgage scoring business to a lower cost rival can weigh on how investors think about future cash flows, even as a new US$2.0b buyback program may support per share value if cash generation holds up.
With the company screening as undervalued on the DCF estimate by 24.2% but scoring only 2 out of 6 on broader valuation checks, Fair Isaac does not screen as a clear bargain when all metrics are considered together.
The issue now is whether the current share price already captures the regulatory and competitive risks around Fair Isaac's scoring franchise or if the intrinsic value estimate still offers a reasonable margin of safety.
The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) approach estimates what Fair Isaac is worth based on the cash it can generate for shareholders. For the latest twelve months, Fair Isaac produced free cash flow of about $873.9m, and the model assumes those cash flows keep growing from this base rather than shrinking or staying flat.
On these projections, the DCF model points to an intrinsic value of about $1,592.76 per share in dollar terms, which is 24.2% above the current share price estimate used in the model, so the stock screens as undervalued on this basis. The recent Federal Housing Finance Agency ruling that opened mortgage scoring to a lower cost rival helps explain why the market is applying a discount even though the cash flow outlook in the model remains positive.
Putting it together, the Discounted Cash Flow view suggests Fair Isaac stock appears undervalued relative to the cash the business is expected to generate, based on the assumptions used in the model.
The P/E ratio is a common way to gauge what investors are willing to pay for each dollar of Fair Isaac's earnings. Fair Isaac trades on a P/E of about 36.8x, compared with a Software industry average of roughly 28.0x and a peer average of 25.1x, so the stock changes hands at a clear premium to both its sector and closer peers.
A tailored fair P/E ratio for Fair Isaac, which takes into account factors such as its margins, size and risk profile, sits lower at about 33.5x. That leaves the current P/E several turns above this fair ratio, indicating that investors are paying more for the stock relative to what the model suggests would be reasonable based on those fundamentals.
On the P/E multiple, Fair Isaac stock currently appears overvalued compared with both sector norms and the more tailored fair ratio estimate.
The Fair Isaac Narrative: What Would Justify Today's Price?
Simply Wall St Narratives pick up where Fair Isaac's valuation puzzle leaves off. They spell out which assumptions on Fair Isaac's growth, margins and earnings would need to hold for the stock to be worth meaningfully more or less than today's price. Each narrative links a fair value estimate to a specific storyline about the company's potential catalysts and risks on the Community page, so you can track over time which version appears closer to how events unfold.
The Fair Isaac community is split between those who see mortgage pressure as a set up for upside and those who think it exposes a weaker future earnings base.
Bull case: 22% undervalued
"The ongoing transition to SaaS and cloud-based delivery, evidenced by double-digit growth in FICO Platform ARR and emphasis on conversion to next-generation AI-driven decisioning solutions, is increasing recurring revenues, supporting margin expansion and greater earnings predictability…"
"Global regulatory trends are shifting towards tighter data privacy and use restrictions, including anticipated U.S. regulations similar to GDPR, which are likely to limit the data inputs available for FICO's analytics and credit scoring models, undermining their accuracy, reducing their relevance to lenders, and leading to lower future revenues and slower growth in the core Scores segment…"
For Fair Isaac, the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) intrinsic value estimate points to meaningful upside, while the P/E and other multiples say the stock already carries a premium price tag. That split reflects different sensitivities, with the DCF leaning on cash flow resilience and the market multiples more exposed to how growth expectations and sentiment reset after regulatory changes. Broader valuation checks remain weak despite the DCF signal, so the key question is whether mortgage and regulatory pressures simply justify a discount or ultimately erode the cash flow base that underpins the intrinsic value case.

rawItems.body:
Never miss an important update on your stock portfolio and cut through the noise. Over 7 million investors trust Simply Wall St to stay informed where it matters for FREE.
-
Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac have released expanded historical loan datasets for FICO Score 10T.
-
The datasets cover real-world mortgage performance under the next-generation FICO scoring model.
-
This move represents a key step in modernizing credit scoring for the US mortgage market.
For Fair Isaac (NYSE:FICO), the expanded datasets from Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac put its FICO Score 10T model more squarely in focus for lenders, investors, and regulators. The company is best known for its credit scoring business, which sits at the center of mortgage underwriting and securitization practices across the US housing finance system.
The release of detailed historical performance data is expected to influence how lenders test, validate, and potentially implement FICO Score 10T over time. Investors tracking Fair Isaac may view this as a notable development in the evolution of credit assessment standards, with practical implications for mortgage risk models, capital allocation, and consumer access to credit.

-

-
✅ Simply Wall St Valuation: Current price is reported as 24.2% below an estimated fair value, suggesting a discount.
-
❌ Recent Momentum: The share price has declined 6.1% over the past 30 days.

Key Considerations
-
📊 The FICO Score 10T datasets from Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac increase transparency around a core Fair Isaac product, which may matter for long term adoption and revenue quality.
-
📊 Watch how quickly mortgage lenders and securitization investors reference FICO Score 10T in underwriting standards, disclosures, and model validation work.
-
⚠️ With one flagged risk around debt levels, consider how much balance sheet flexibility Fair Isaac has if the mortgage market is slow to adjust to new scoring models.
